answer_inventory.evidence: An ETag lets the client validate stored JSON
The server includes an ETag with its response. On a later conditional GET, the client sends that value in If-None-Match.
If the tag matches the selected representation, an otherwise successful GET returns 304 Not Modified with no response body, allowing reuse of the stored body.
If it does not match, a successful GET returns 200 OK with the current JSON.
To allow reuse without validation, set an appropriate freshness policy, such as Cache-Control: max-age=60, subject to the other caching rules.
The client can reuse the cached response while fresh; this does not guarantee unchanged underlying data for 60 seconds.
